machine.name: Home Environment Safety Response Interconnect
machine.description: Published personal-health bridge bus that composes home environment safety, food access, adolescent behavioral health, social isolation, and fall-safety context into a compact fan-out lane for urgent housing safety response, utility/housing resource support, health-hazard behavioral follow-up, and stable monitoring. PE owns source composition and writes the compact input lane; RE evaluates this machine as ordinary vector state.

metadata.domain: Personal Health - Published Environment Safety Response Bus
metadata.author: Reality Engine

publishedDomainBus.name: Personal Health Environment Safety Response Bus
publishedDomainBus.description: Domain-level published bus for home environment safety, food access, adolescent behavioral health, social support, and fall-safety interconnection.

downstreamConsumers.purpose: dispatch care coordination agent for housing safety support
behavioral health signal monitoring under housing adversity
guardrail inequitable housing and family-support burden
govern urgent family housing safety escalation
resident intake triage for housing safety
case routing for housing and utility supports
air quality particulate and VOC monitoring

fanOutPolicy.notes: PE selects consumers from outputMatchesAny after RE emits the bus output. Urgent housing safety response, utility/housing resource support, health-hazard behavioral follow-up, and stable monitoring intentionally fan out to different consumers.

writeBack.name: localAIStack environment safety response resolver completion
semantics: urgent housing safety response resolved or acknowledged
utility housing resource support resolved or acknowledged
health hazard behavioral follow-up resolved or acknowledged
environment stable monitoring resolved or acknowledged

sourceMapping.name: localAIStack environment safety response resolver completion

localAIResolver.notes: Resolver metadata is consumed by PE startup configuration. It intentionally does not create metadata.agentBinding because this bridge machine is not an agent-dispatcher and RE should see only ordinary vector state.

rules.description: URGENT_HOUSING_SAFETY_RESPONSE: unsafe housing with household, behavioral, social, or fall co-risk at [4432:4436]
UTILITY_HOUSING_RESOURCE_SUPPORT: utility or housing resource support needed at [4432:4436]
HEALTH_HAZARD_BEHAVIORAL_FOLLOWUP: housing health hazard with behavioral, social, or fall follow-up need at [4432:4436]
ENVIRONMENT_STABLE_MONITORING: environment and support lanes stable at [4432:4436]

governance.notes: Published PE-composed bridge bus for environment safety response. RE evaluates only vector state; PE owns source provenance and completion ingestion.

sequences.name: Unsafe housing + behavioral/fall co-risk -> urgent housing safety response

metadata.description: Unsafe housing coincides with food crisis, adolescent crisis, severe isolation, and fall co-risk.

metadata.action: Route urgent housing safety response, care coordination, family stabilization, utility/rental assistance, and built-space incident follow-up.

sequences.name: Utility failure + resource barriers -> utility housing resource support

metadata.description: Utility failure is active with food assistance need and social withdrawal, but not yet an unsafe-housing crisis.

metadata.action: Route LIHEAP/utility assistance, rental support, case routing, and family resource support.

sequences.name: Health hazard + adolescent stress -> health hazard behavioral follow-up

metadata.description: Housing health hazard risk is active with food insecurity, adolescent elevated stress, isolation risk, or fall vulnerability.

metadata.action: Route air/water quality, adolescent behavioral, maternal-child, and care-coordination follow-up before crisis escalation.

sequences.name: Safe environment + stable household supports -> environment stable monitoring

metadata.description: Environment, food access, adolescent health, social support, and fall-safety lanes are stable.

metadata.action: Continue lightweight built-space, family routine, and water-access monitoring.
